prompt: A clean, straight-on GRAPHIC of a short secret word written in the PIGPEN (Freemason) CIPHER: a single horizontal row of exactly six pigpen glyphs, left to right, one glyph per letter, dark strokes on a plain light card. In the pigpen cipher each letter is drawn as a fragment of a grid: a bracket made of straight line segments (some combination of a top, bottom, left and/or right side, forming an open-cornered box) for the tic-tac-toe letters, or a V-shaped wedge for the X-grid letters, and some letters additionally carry a single DOT inside the glyph. Encode the plaintext word "PLACID" glyph by glyph using the standard pigpen cipher, drawing each letter's exact glyph: the correct combination of sides (and the dot where the letter requires one). Draw the six glyphs evenly spaced in one row, each glyph clearly separated, thick clean strokes, high contrast. Do not draw any letters of the alphabet or any other text — only the six pigpen glyphs.
